column1: # *** SANCHO LLERENA'S OWN CHILDREN, AT CANELONES - reached 14 September 2026. ***
# Catedral Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe, Villa de los Canelones. Found through FULL-TEXT, which reads
# the handwriting; none of these acts is name-indexed under LERENA.
# The family's home town. Justa Pastora is "natural de Canelones" in her son's 1831 act; Sancho
# appears at Canelones as a sworn witness in the marriage-investigation files; and here are his
# children being baptised there.

*** DOMINGA JOSEFA LLERENA Fernandez ***

column3: 15 May 1804, by Presbitero Don Manuel Acevedo, teniente cura
column4: *** "hija legitima de SANCHO LLERENA y de MARIA FERNANDEZ; fueron los Padrinos Joseph Ponteceli y Agueda Rivero, todos VECINOS DE LA MISMA VILLA" ***

column1: # *** WHAT THIS SETTLES. ***
# 1. *** THE DOMINGA LERENA WHO STOOD GODMOTHER AT THE CATEDRAL IN 1833 IS THIS WOMAN *** - a
#    daughter of Sancho, aged 29 that year, standing for her sister Justa Pastora's child. The
#    archive guessed "almost certainly her sister or cousin"; it is the sister.
# 2. *** SANCHO IS NOW ATTESTED IN 1804 *** - twenty-seven years earlier than any record this archive
#    had two days ago, and thirty-two earlier than his son's marriage petition. And the act calls him
#    SANCHO, not Francisco.
# 3. *** CANELONES IS THE FAMILY'S TOWN, not merely a place in a published tree. *** "Todos vecinos de
#    la misma Villa" - the parents and both godparents are neighbours there.
# A FOURTH SPELLING, noted for the record: the machine transcript's name list renders him
# *** "SANCIO Llerena" *** on this act. Sancio joins Lerena, Llerena, Lorena, Serena and Lerina in the
# list of ways this family has been written. It is the same alternation the 1869 Uruguayan census
# already showed for him.
# ---- AND SANCHO IN PERSON, TWICE MORE AT CANELONES ----
# *** AS A GODFATHER AT A CONFIRMATION, 1804. *** Catedral Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe, Confirmation
# Records 1804, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-73LL-2. The list runs:
#     "Jose, ESCLAVO DE MANUEL LOPEZ - padrino SANCHO LLERENA"
# He stood godfather at the confirmation of an ENSLAVED MAN. The act is recorded here as it stands,
# without softening: slavery was legal in the Banda Oriental in 1804 and the registers name the
# enslaved by a forename and an owner. What it says about Sancho is that he was a man of the town
# asked to sponsor, and that is the third distinct role he holds in these Canelones books.
# *** AS A SWORN WITNESS, in the marriage-investigation files 1776-1806 *** - ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2Z-W45W:
#     "presento por testigo en esta Vicaria a SANCHO LLERENA, a quien se le recivio Juramento que lo
#      hizo ... bajo del cual prometio decir verdad de lo que supiere y le fuere preguntado"
# So at Canelones he is a FATHER (1804), a GODFATHER (1804) and a SWORN WITNESS (1776-1806). Two days
# ago he was a name on a user-built tree that two acts appeared to contradict.
